A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLAME research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original medication-recommendation experiments, including MIMIC-III comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–2, generalization results in Fig. 5, and training curves in Fig. 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds test-set medication-edit statistics and two refinement examples in Section 5.4 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The two-stage classifier/refinement pipeline, step-wise GRPO, reward shaping, knowledge fusion, and inference procedure are retained. Added descriptions of the candidate vocabulary and classifier initialization document the method without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-III for training and evaluation, MIMIC-IV and eICU for generalization, and TWOSIDES for DDI information. The new refinement analysis uses existing MIMIC-III test data without introducing another task or test environment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Table 1, Fig. 5, and the Table 2 ablations is unchanged. Newly discussed DAPO and StepGRPO are related work, with no reported head-to-head evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 adds test-set edit-count summaries and correctness assessment of 28 edited Piperacillin-containing lists, with two displayed cases. This introduces a limited diagnostic assessment; existing splits, preprocessing, training budgets, and benchmark metrics remain unchanged. The new correctness-assessment procedure is only briefly specified.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 examines what list-wise refinement contributes through edit-frequency analysis, antibiotic-related corrections, and two case studies in Table 3. Existing component ablations, generalization tests, and training-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, evaluation confidence intervals, or significance tests. Fig. 6 retains the same reward and reward_std training plots; the new edit statistics do not introduce uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figs. 5–6 retain their results, including FLAME's 0.4836 Jaccard and 0.6408 F1. New results include 20.83 initial drugs and approximately 2.03 edits per patient, classifier DDI of 0.1336, 89% correctness across 28 edited Piperacillin-containing lists, and two case outputs. The stated 82.1% relative refinement gain is calculated from unchanged ablation scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, reward-shaping equations, Theorem 4.1, and Appendix A's policy-equivalence proof are unchanged in substance. No new theorem, assumption, derivation, or proof correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about fine-grained list-wise alignment, knowledge fusion, recommendation accuracy, safety control, and generalization. The added analysis supports these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly explains small aggregate gains through the lightweight nature of refinement, interprets antibiotic edits as correcting redundancies and omissions, and contextualizes GRPO's contribution relative to the refinement gain. The limitations and broader-impact discussions in Appendices D–E remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly identifies the candidate set as all unique medications in processed training data, and Appendix B.1 adds a concrete parsed clinical-note example. Hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and the code link are retained. The expanded classifier description leaves unresolved the existing Beta-backbone description in the main text versus Alpha in Appendix C.1.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds comparisons with DAPO and StepGRPO concerning localized rewards and process supervision, while Section 2.1 adds three recommendation references. This extends the existing positioning without replacing it. The flow-guided tuning reference's preprint-to-proceedings update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.4 and acknowledgments, expands several explanations, and makes localized wording and publication-footer edits. The existing narrative, section sequence, method exposition, and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the color-coded case-study Table 3 and a boxed clinical-note example, expands Fig. 1's caption, and reflows subsequent material. The original dataset-statistics Table 3 becomes Table 4 without substantive changes; the six existing figures and main quantitative tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The new edit statistics and concrete cases make the small ablation gains easier to interpret, while the related-work comparisons and input documentation improve clarity. These are limited gains: the principal experimental and theoretical evidence is unchanged, and the 28-list correctness analysis lacks enough procedural detail and uncertainty reporting to establish broader clinical benefits.
